```{r include=FALSE}
library("skimr")
library("readr")
library("here")
```



## Load & Inspect

In this phase, we load the dataset and perform an initial inspection to understand its structure, size, and basic properties.
first we need to load our dataset. beacuse in first 20 lines of dataset is for header section, so we sould skip it.
```{r}
my_data <- readr::read_csv('D:/climetr/climetr_analysis/datasets/POWER_Point_Daily_20130101_20251123_032d86N_059d22E_LST_Birjand.csv', skip = 20)
```


then we should inspect it to find any unusual values and know our data better.
```{r}
skim_without_charts(my_data)
```
in dataset the values for missing source data that cannot be computed or is outside of the sources availability range is -999, so we shuld mark them as na.
columns of year should be a string type columns.

check -> T2M_MIN ≤ T2M ≤ T2M_MAX

## Cleaning

In this phase, we clean the dataset by handling missing values, removing invalid entries, and ensuring data consistency.

## Feature Preparation

In this phase, we convert column names into clear, consistent, and human-readable labels to improve usability during analysis.

## Feature Engineering

In this phase, we create new informative variables from the existing columns to support deeper analysis and modeling.

## Save Clean Data

Finally, we save the cleaned and prepared dataset for later use in analysis and visualization.
